HOW TO FLY

Controls

Course rules

Follow the glowing line and fly through the gates in order. Altitude drains as you fly. Lime boost rings and light beams lift you.

Low park sections weave between trees. Look for bronze sculptures framing gates and boost rings, and a wooded park around the finish.

Follow the rings through collectors, connecting tunnels and shafts. Moving air supports a level glide; rising shafts have an updraft. Watch for rotating poles and solid fan hubs. Wall fans push air or water along visible streams; steer around them to avoid being pushed sideways. Ordinary green water, walls and obstacles cause a crash.

Tunnels can split into two passages above or below the water. In dry tunnels, a red skull painted on a wooden barricade marks the dead end. Underwater, follow the cyan lights into the correct passage.

Red painted downward arrows mark flooded mazes. Dive below the barricades; the entrance shutter closes behind you. Follow the bright cyan lights through the forks to the single air outlet, and dodge the pipes underwater.

Your 26 seconds of oxygen refill in air; running out causes a crash and full course restart. Unlit sections fade into darkness and back out again. A flashlight lights up nearby obstacles and reaches much farther underwater.

A missed gate adds 2 seconds. A crash adds 3 seconds and returns you to your last gate.

A missed gate adds 2 seconds. Any crash restarts the entire course with a fresh timer.

Flying far off course warns you, then returns you with an extra 5 seconds.

Look for spinning stars tucked in harder detours beside the route: 1 on Easy and Medium, 2 on Hard, 3 on Extreme. Fly close, then finish the course to save them. A checkpoint crash keeps your finds for that attempt; returning to the menu, restarting or reloading discards unfinished finds. Saved stars are shared across difficulties for that course and become faint outlines. Stars are optional and add no time bonus or penalty.

Star shop

Open Shop from the menu or pause screen. Spend 2 stars on a Lift Boost, then press Space or tap LIFT during flight for a burst of height. Carry three; use one per flight. Unused boosts stay in your inventory.

Using one makes the flight assisted: stars still save when you finish, but medals, best times and Extreme unlocks require flying without a purchased boost.

A Flashlight costs 5 stars for five Sewer flights. Equip or unequip it in the Shop. An equipped Sewer Fly uses one charge, lasting until you crash, finish or leave. Pause keeps the same light; surface flights keep your saved charges.

Difficulty

  • Easy: open avenues and regular rings; no side streets or course obstacles.
  • Medium: a few wider side streets and obstacles; regular rings.
  • Hard: more narrow turns and obstacles; smaller rings.
  • Extreme: tight streets and wooded parks, smaller rings and faster flight.

Higher difficulties narrow the tunnels and rings and add more pipe obstacles, dirt banks and rotating shaft poles. Pole speeds and directions change with difficulty. Hard and Extreme add more flooded mazes; Extreme also raises flight speed. Sewer times and Extreme unlocks are saved separately from the surface.

Screen orientation

The game requests a fixed landscape side. If the browser rotates anyway, the game view turns back to the side used at Fly. Browser bars may still rotate.

To stop the screen rotating at all, turn on the phone's rotation lock, open the game in portrait and tap play sideways. The game then turns itself to the side you hold the phone.

Courses and times

Copy a course code or share the page URL to fly the same course and difficulty again. Your best time is saved in this browser. Medals use your flight time plus penalties. Earn Gold or Diamond on Hard to unlock Extreme for that course.

Diamond matches the clean reference run with no extra time allowance. Keep every gate, cut corners where there is room and use clean dives to gain speed.
